newsitem.title: USA: US black group says Texaco agreement 'first step'.
newsitem.headline: US black group says Texaco agreement 'first step'.

text.p: The U.S. National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) on Friday welcomed Texaco Inc's settlement of a 1994 race discrimination suit.

Still, the settlement was just a "first step," and the NAACP was still prepared to move ahead with its threatened divestiture of Texaco stock if negotiations with the company over the next few weeks failed to produce desired results, the group said.
"The NAACP is in this process for the long haul, and we will continue over the next two to three weeks our discussions with Texaco," the group said in a statement.

"Should those negotiations fail to bring about a specific plan of action on Texaco's part, we are still prepared to move ahead with a nationwide coordinated stock divestiture campaign," the statement said.

Beyond the immediate settlement of the lawsuit, hiring goals, promotional opportunities and procurement practices were vital parts of creating equal opportunity and fairness at Texaco, the statement said.
